title: Dedicated autoscaling: burst controls and utilization reporting
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Dedicated customers require controlled short-term burst capacity while preserving guaranteed throughput and predictable billing. This PR introduces burst controls to the Dedicated autoscaler and expands utilization reporting for fleet-level and pool-level visibility. The core changes add new FleetConfig fields (burst_capacity, burst_duration_seconds, burst_cooldown_seconds, soft_utilization_limit) and server-side enforcement logic in the dedicated controller that allows short-lived transient overcommit with automatic cooldown and accounting. We also wire new telemetry metrics (dedicated_fleet_burst_used, dedicated_pool_utilization, dedicated_pool_tail_latency_p50_p95_p99) to the observability pipeline and add Grafana dashboard panels and alert rules. Backwards compatibility: default values preserve existing autoscaler behavior; burst is opt-in per-fleet via feature flag or explicit config. Rollout plan: gated canary on two low-risk customers, monitor utilization and billing delta for 48 hours, then ramp. Testing: unit tests for controller logic, e2e load tests in perf-canary, simulation harness added to benchmark-lab to validate cooldowns and billing tags. Docs: console UI and API docs updated with examples and recommended policies. Impact: improves short-term capacity for spiky workloads while avoiding unbounded scaling costs and provides operators with clearer utilization signals to tune reserved capacity.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can you clarify billing tags for burst usage so we can tie costs back to customers?
Ava Martinez: Burst usage is emitted with billing_tag=burst and includes start/end timestamps; billing teams can aggregate by billing_tag.
Maya Singh: Add a safety net to prevent burst from exceeding max_replicas when hardware is constrained.
Ava Martinez: Added hard cap checks in burst_accounting.go and an explicit validation that ensures burst_capacity <= (max_replicas - min_replicas).
Liang Zhou: Integration tests were flaky on CI due to timing of cooldown windows; can we stabilize by mocking time or extending windows in tests?
Ava Martinez: Switched problematic tests to a simulated clock and reduced wall-clock timing in CI, added a note in tests about simulation mode.

release_notes: Added burst_capacity and burst_duration_seconds to FleetConfig to allow controlled transient overcommit for dedicated fleets
New telemetry metrics: dedicated_fleet_burst_used, dedicated_pool_utilization, dedicated_pool_tail_latency_p50_p95_p99
Console UI: Fleet settings page has Burst Configuration with recommended defaults and an opt-in toggle
Rollout: feature is opt-in and will be rolled out behind a feature flag; customers will not see behavior changes unless they update FleetConfig
